purpose: Methotrexate is used to treat certain types of cancer, rheumatoid arthritis, and skin conditions like psoriasis. It helps reduce inflammation and slow down the overactive processes in your body that cause these diseases. Your doctor may also prescribe it for other inflammatory conditions like lupus or psoriatic arthritis.
how_it_works: Methotrexate works by slowing down the growth of certain cells in your body that are dividing too quickly, like cancer cells or the immune cells that cause inflammation. It does this by blocking a key vitamin called folate that those fast-growing cells need to survive and multiply. This helps calm down your immune system and reduce the damage it causes to your joints or skin.
common_side_effects: Nausea, vomiting, or upset stomach are very common, especially right after taking a dose. You may also notice mouth sores, fatigue, headache, or dizziness. Some people experience hair thinning or a loss of appetite. Taking folic acid (a B vitamin) as directed by your doctor can help reduce some of these side effects.
warnings: Methotrexate can cause serious liver damage over time, so your doctor will do regular blood tests to check your liver. It can also lower your white blood cell count, making it harder for your body to fight infections — call your doctor right away if you develop a fever or signs of infection. This medication must NOT be taken during pregnancy as it can cause serious birth defects or miscarriage. Never drink alcohol while taking methotrexate. Take it ONLY once a week unless directed otherwise — taking it daily by mistake can be life-threatening.
typical_dosing: For arthritis or psoriasis, methotrexate is usually taken ONCE a week — not every day. The dose typically starts low, around 7.5 mg to 15 mg per week, and may be gradually increased by your doctor. It comes as a tablet you swallow or as an injection given under the skin. Always take it on the same day each week, and your doctor will likely have you take folic acid on the other days to protect your body.
